data.current_description:
Queues a full export of every website running one technology and returns straight away with a `report_id`. Generation takes minutes, so nothing useful could be returned synchronously. Poll `GET /v1/tech-lookup/lists/{id}` until `status` is `ready`, then follow `download_url`.

Costs **1 standard credit**, flat, no matter how large the list. Asking for the same technology again inside the same billing period is free. One credit buys that technology for the period, so a nightly refresh costs one credit a month, not one a night.

This spends STANDARD credits, not the bulk-lookup credits the other endpoints use. `GET /v1/me` reports both balances.

Nothing is charged when the request is refused: an unknown technology, or a filter combination that matches no websites, both return an error with the wallet untouched.

Rate limit: 6 requests per minute, counted per API token. Going over returns 429 with `error_code: rate_limited` and a `Retry-After` header in seconds. A 429 costs no credits. Traffic is also subject to a higher shared ceiling per network address, applied before authentication.
data.summary_suggestion: Queue a full technology list export
data.description_suggestion:
Queues an asynchronous full export of all websites running a specified technology. Returns immediately with a `report_id` for polling. The export generation takes several minutes; poll `GET /v1/tech-lookup/lists/{id}` until `status` is `ready`, then download via the returned `download_url`.

**Billing:** Costs 1 standard credit (flat rate, regardless of list size). Requesting the same technology again within the same billing period is free. Uses standard credits, not bulk-lookup credits; check `GET /v1/me` for both balances. No charge is applied if the request fails (unknown technology or no matching websites).

**Polling:** After receiving the `report_id`, poll the status endpoint every few seconds initially, then back off as generation progresses.

**Rate limit:** 6 requests per minute per API token. Exceeding returns 429 with `error_code: rate_limited` and `Retry-After` header.

data.current_description:
Tells you whether the export is `queued`, `ready` or `failed`, and once ready gives you `download_url` plus the row counts.

Free, so polling is fine. Check every few seconds early on, then back off.

**Read `truncated` before you trust the file as complete.** Plans cap how many rows an export may contain, and the ceiling is 1,000,000 even on unlimited plans. When `truncated` is true, `result_count` is how many websites matched and `exported_rows` is how many the file actually holds; `withheld_rows` is the difference.

A `failed` list has already had its credit refunded automatically.

Rate limit: 120 requests per minute, counted per API token. Going over returns 429 with `error_code: rate_limited` and a `Retry-After` header in seconds. A 429 costs no credits. Traffic is also subject to a higher shared ceiling per network address, applied before authentication.
data.description_suggestion:
Retrieves the current status of a technology list export identified by `id` (from the `report_id` returned by POST /v1/tech-lookup/lists). Returns the export status (`queued`, `ready`, or `failed`), and when ready, provides the `download_url` and row counts.

**Response fields:** `status` indicates the export state; `download_url` is available when `status` is `ready`; `result_count` shows total matching websites; `exported_rows` shows rows in the file; `downloads_remaining` indicates how many times the file can still be downloaded.

**Truncation:** Check the `truncated` field before trusting the export as complete. When `truncated` is true, the export hit the plan's row limit (max 1,000,000 rows); `withheld_rows` shows how many websites were excluded.

**Refunds:** Failed exports automatically refund their credit.

**Cost:** Free. Safe to poll frequently early on, then back off as generation progresses.

**Rate limit:** 120 requests per minute per API token.

data.current_description:
Rate limited well below the polling endpoints, because these files reach 1.2 GiB. Each list may also be fetched a limited number of times in total; the status endpoint reports `downloads_remaining` so you can see it coming, and a list past its ceiling returns `403 download_limit_reached` rather than a 429, because retrying will not help.

Attempts are counted, not completed transfers, so a dropped connection still spends one. An expired file (`410`) does not.

Streams the finished file. Large lists come back as CSV and small ones as XLSX, whichever survives the row count. Returns 409 while the list is still `queued`, so a client that polls correctly never sees it.

Free and repeatable for as long as the file is retained.

Rate limit: 10 requests per minute, counted per API token. Going over returns 429 with `error_code: rate_limited` and a `Retry-After` header in seconds. A 429 costs no credits. Traffic is also subject to a higher shared ceiling per network address, applied before authentication.
data.summary_suggestion: Download a completed technology list export
data.description_suggestion:
Downloads the completed technology list export file identified by `id`. The file is streamed directly and format depends on size: CSV for large lists, XLSX for small lists.

**Prerequisites:** The export must have `status: ready` (check via GET /v1/tech-lookup/lists/{id} first). Attempting to download while `status` is `queued` returns 409.

**Download limits:** Each list has a maximum number of downloads allowed; check `downloads_remaining` from the status endpoint to monitor availability. Exceeding the limit returns `403 download_limit_reached` (not retryable).

**File retention:** Files are retained for a limited time. Expired files return `410`. Attempts are counted even if the transfer fails; only expired files don't consume an attempt.

**Cost:** Free. Repeatable as long as the file is retained.

**Rate limit:** 10 requests per minute per API token (stricter than polling endpoints due to large file sizes up to 1.2 GiB).
